gen-silkscreen-gf-gotu: Retro through and through, Silkscreen strings its letters out like spaghetti. Gotu, a plain sans with light stroke contrast and open e crossbars, gives that lo-fi heading something sturdy to lean on.
gen-silkscreen-gf-ibm-plex-sans-thai-loo: IBM Plex Sans Thai Looped leaves its curves unclosed. IBM Plex Sans Thai Looped and Silkscreen both skip hairlines, so nothing vanishes in glare, from the retro heading down to the text.
gen-silkscreen-gf-kanchenjunga: Lo-fi spaghetti letters, Silkscreen sets the retro mood up top. Kanchenjunga, a sans drawn with the steady line of a technical drafting pen, feels precise and contemporary next to all that spacing.
gen-silkscreen-gf-lxgw-marker-gothic: Lo-fi letters bent from a single wire: that is Silkscreen. LXGW Marker Gothic takes over with a wide-open c and stems just outweighing its hairlines, giving the wire-bent heading a smooth, modest partner.
gen-silkscreen-gf-mingzat: Retro first: Silkscreen looks laser-cut, with one cutting width. Mingzat, a contemporary sans, lets paragraphs unfold loose and low in contrast, its curvy letters feeling unclamped from line to line.
gen-silkscreen-gf-moderustic: Moderustic reads like curves traced with a broad nib, left unfinished. Silkscreen, with straight-edged, constant strokes and a retro lo-fi spirit, makes a crisp counterpoint to the soft, contemporary body beneath.
gen-silkscreen-gf-molengo: Molengo reads crisp, thanks to the wide gaps between its letters. Down a full page it stays low in contrast, a sensible foil for Silkscreen, whose spaghetti-line letters keep the heading lo-fi.
gen-silkscreen-gf-mona-sans: Neutral in mood, Mona Sans opens each letter like a door ajar. Paragraphs in it flow smoothly and low in contrast, sitting beneath the constant-width, sign-painter's brush look of Silkscreen.
gen-silkscreen-gf-monda: Silkscreen spaces every letter apart, a spaghetti line of unit-width strokes. But where the heading goes for lo-fi flair, Monda, a sans, keeps every small counter unclogged and approachable.
gen-silkscreen-gf-mooli: Retro to its core, Silkscreen strings out letters with a single unbroken line weight from terminals to junctions. Mooli, a sans, takes over the reading with open round letters.
